newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea fin min eases central bank responsibilities.
newsitem.headline: SKorea fin min eases central bank responsibilities.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economy Ministry said on Thursday it would eliminate from its draft financial reforms a clause making the head of the central bank responsible for meeting annual inflation targets.
This was among the ministry's revisions to its draft reforms, which addressed several of the more controversial provisions.
The ministry on June 16 said the central bank governor would be asked to set annual inflation targets and would be held responsible for meeting those targets.
But the latest ministry statement said the government had revised parts of the earlier draft to enhance the authority and independence of the central bank.

As earlier proposed, the central bank's governor would head the Monetary Board, which decides monetary policies. But the revision dropped the link between the board and the government by eliminating a clause giving the finance minister the right to influence the board's decisions.
Under new central bank laws, the monetary board would independently set monetary policies, which would be implemented by the Bank of Korea, the statement said.
The central bank would govern settlement-linked business and other administrative activities related with monetary policy.

The three existing supervisory bodies for the banking, securities and insurance sectors will be integrated into a unified organisation under the prime minister's direct control. But the number of watchdog committee members would be raised to nine from an earlier seven by adding more professionals.

"I believe the revision will clarify the authority and independence of the central bank and improve the effectiveness of the unifying supervisory body," Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters.
He stressed the importance of financial reform to solve structural problems of the nation's economy.
Legislation to implement the finance ministry's plans needs to be approved by the National Assembly.
"I plan to submit the financial reform legislation in early August to the National Assembly, based on the revised draft," Kang said. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
